chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) went out while he was in grief, so an Angel came to him, and with him were the keys to the treasures of the earth. He said: 'O Muhammad! These are the keys to the treasures of the earth. Your Lord says to you: 'Open and take from them whatever you wish, without anything being diminished in My Presence.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The world is the house of the one who has no house for himself, and for it there is a collection for the one who has no intellect for himself.' The Angel said: 'By the One who sent you with the Truth as a Prophet, I have heard this speech from an Angel saying it in the fourth heaven, when I was given the keys.'

key_terms.مَفَاتِيحُ خَزَائِنِ الْأَرْضِ: Keys to the treasures of the earth
key_terms.مَنْ لَا عَقْلَ لَهُ: The one who has no intellect

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the nature of the world when offered its treasures?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) declines the offer of earthly treasures not out of inability, but to demonstrate the spiritual superiority of detachment (*zuhd*) over material accumulation. This incident underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Prophet’s conscious choice of the Hereafter, reinforcing the concept that true wealth lies in divine proximity rather than worldly power. The Angel’s confirmation highlights the cosmic significance of this choice, linking the Prophet’s earthly conduct to the celestial realm.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> who said:

‘The Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> came out and he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> was in grief. So an Angel came over to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, and with him were keys to the treasures of the earth, and he said: ‘O Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>! These are keys to the treasures of the earth. Your<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is Saying to you<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> “Open and take from it whatever you<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> so desire to from without there being a reduction of anything in My Presence”’.

So Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘The world is a house for the one what has no house for him, and for it there is a collection for the one who has no intellect for him’. So the Angel said: ‘By the One<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Who Sent you<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> with the Truth as a Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, I had heard this speech from an Angel saying it in the fourth sky, when I was given the keys’’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hassan ibn Rashid from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Once, the Holy Prophet came out very depressed. An angel came to him with the key to the treasures of the earth and said, ‘O Muhammad, these are the keys to the treasures of the earth and your Lord says, “Open these treasures and take whatever you want. It will not cause any reduction in your reward with Me.”

The Messenger of Allah then said, ‘This world is home for the homeless. Only those who have no power of reason accumulate for this world.’ The angel then said, ‘I swear by the One Who has sent you with truth as a prophet that I heard what you just said from an angel saying it in the fourth heaven at the time these keys were given to me.’”
